Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
Prefixes are unstressed except anti- and non-, so unreliable is /ˌʌn.rɪˈlaɪ.ə.bəl/ with the stress on the root, exactly as in reliable.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Prefixes & Negative Forms.

Negate with a prefix when the word has a stable opposite (unfair, illegal, disagree). Use not when the negation is temporary or contrastive (the report is not finished, but not unfinishable). Never write unlegal or inlegal: the prefix is fixed by the root, so learn the pairs.

un- — negates, native roots: unreliable, unclear, unfair
in- / il- / im- / ir- — negates, Latinate roots: incapable, illegal, impossible, irregular
dis- — negates or reverses an action: disagree, disconnect, disqualify
mis- — wrongly: misinterpret, misreport, mislead
anti- — against: anticompetitive, antidumping
non- — not of that type: non-binding, non-renewable
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'The data is ___ complete.'
2. Which word means 'quoted wrongly'?
3. Which prefix assimilates before p?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

unreliable — The source proved unreliable. (un- before a native root.)
illegal — The payment was illegal. (il- before l.)
misinterpret — The press misinterpreted the ruling. (mis- means wrongly.)
What do you observe?

The prefix carries the negation, so the word class stays the same: reliable and unreliable are both adjectives. The choice among un-, in-, dis- and mis- is lexical, and in- assimilates to il- before l, im- before m and p, and ir- before r.
1. Does a negative prefix change the word class?
2. Which prefix fits 'legal'?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can explain how prefixes change meaning.

Success criteria:
- I can choose between un-, in-, dis- and mis-.
- I can use il-, im- and ir- before the right letters.
- I can say why a prefix is better than not + word here.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The payment was inlegal (wrong prefix for the root) → ✅ The payment was illegal
❌ The audit was not completeable (not + derived adjective) → ✅ The audit was incomplete
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The evidence is uncontested but thin.
Two members disagreed with the ruling.
The figure was misquoted in three outlets.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where compound nouns carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Compound Nouns. Decide the head noun first, then the modifier, then the spelling: two words by default, one word if the language has closed it, hyphens only when the compound modifies another noun
